To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the following antibodies were found to react only with thymocytes: OKT 6, OKT 10, OKT 11, and MAS 036b.
Fifteen monoclonal anti-T-cell antibodies were studied by immunocytochemistry in thymic and non-thymic tissue.

OKT 9 is a marker for haemopoietic stem and precursor cells in fetal life, OKT 6, OKT 10 and MAS 036b are markers for thymocytes and OKT 4 and OKT 8 are markers for mature T-lymphocyte populations in tonsils and thymus.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and characterization of monoclonal antibodies (MAb) directed against T-cell surface antigens and the use of these antibodies for immunohistochemical studies on normal human thymus and tonsils and on T-cell lymphomas.
the development and application of a new type of monoclonal antibodies, the so-called monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) against T-lymphocyte antigens.
the identification and characterization of T-cell antigens by monoclonal antibodies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these 15 monoclonal antibodies react with T-lymphocyte antigens.
OKT 9 and OKT 10 are not T-cell specific, OKT 6, 8–9, 8–10, and 8–11 are restricted to T-cell lymphocytes, and that the remaining monoclonal antibodies studied label T-cells and B-cells.
OKT 3 and OKT 4 are most useful in identifying T-cells in thymus or in tonsillar interstitial tissue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
OKT 9, OKT 10, OKT 6, OKT 3 and OKT 4 reacted with thymic lymphocytes, OKT 9 with hemopoietal stem cells in fetal liver, OKT 4 with a subpopulation of interfollicullar lymphocytes in tonsils.
OKT 9 and OKT 10 are markers for hemopoietic cells, OKT 6, MAS 036 b and OKT 4 for thymocytes, OKT 3 and NEI 016 for mature thymocytes, and OKT 5 and OKT 8 for mature T-lympho-cytes in tonsils.
the T-lymphocyte antigens are not restricted to T-cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of monoclonal antibodies to study the human immune system has been greatly facilitated by the availability of the human genome sequence, and by advances in the technology of antibody production and characterization, as well as in immunohistochemistry and flow cytometry.

the TCR is a highly variable molecule that can be used to define the T-cell receptor repertoire in a given individual, and that it can be used as an immunological marker to define the phenotype of T-cells.
the TCR repertoire of the thymus is not as diverse as previously thought.
